about.text: Butter is a dairy product made from the fat and protein components of churned cream. It is a semi-solid emulsion at room temperature, consisting of approximately 81% butterfat. It is used at room temperature as a spread, melted as a condiment, and used as a fat in baking, sauce-making, pan frying, and other cooking procedures.

how.text: Pasteurise hot, ripen cold for the right fat crystals, churn, drain, work, salt.

steps.note: Cooled by a temperature programme set to the fat's iodine value (for example 8-21-16 °C for iodine value 28-29; 6-17-11 °C for 35-37), as in a study aged 10 °C for 17 h.
The fat globule membranes break and the fat clumps into grains.
Unsalted, salted or extra salted; sprinkled on in a batch churn, added as a slurry in a continuous buttermaker.

steps.name: work
steps.note: The grains are worked until no water droplets are visible, the salt worked in.

facts.v: 35–40 % fat cream is typical for churning
Milk solids-not-fat at most 2 %; German unsalted butter at least 82 % fat
Butter used to be washed with water after churning, rarely done today
Cultured butter smells of diacetyl, sweet butter tastes of cream; cultured gives richer aroma and higher yield but more oxidation risk, and a much more acid buttermilk
